body.statement: Establish or refute the following assertion using \(H_{\mathrm{WE}}\). There exist universal \(c_0,c_1,c_2\in(0,1)\) such that, for every \(0<\alpha\le1/4\) and every \((w,q)\) satisfying \(\sum_{l=1}^Lq_ls_l^2=1\) and \(\|s\|_\infty\sqrt{x_\alpha}\le c_0\), the interval \([-c_2\sqrt{x_\alpha},c_2\sqrt{x_\alpha}]\) is contained in \(\mathcal T_{\mathrm{tilt}}\), and every measurable \(\Lambda(O,R)\) obeys \[\inf_{|t|\le c_2\sqrt{x_\alpha}}Q_t\{T(V)\in\Lambda(O,R)\}\ge1-\alpha\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\sup_{|t|\le c_2\sqrt{x_\alpha}}\mathbb E_{Q_t}[\operatorname{len}\{\Lambda(O,R)\}]\ge c_1\min\{1,\sqrt{Sx_\alpha}\}.\] Here \(Q_t=\pi_t\otimes P_K\otimes\operatorname{Uniform}[0,1]\): every probability and expectation integrates \(V\sim\pi_t\), \(K\sim P_K\) independently of \(V\), and the external \(R\) independently of \((V,K)\). The assertion is solely the posterior-spread inequality. The pointwise-coverage and worst-case-to-prior-average transfer for \(\Lambda_\Gamma\) is supplied by \(\mathrm{lem{:}hard\text{-}subexperiment\text{-}embedding}\), not assumed here.
body.justification: The fully specified prior family and joint law make the first-class lower-bound bottleneck falsifiable for centered, uncentered, deterministic, and externally randomized intervals.
body.gap: CaiLow2004 and ArmstrongKolesar2018 obtain modulus lower bounds in Gaussian experiments, while FelixGarciaSousa2025 treats one-parameter discrete families; none proves posterior spread for a weighted nonidentical erasure experiment with compact block outcomes.
body.consumer: A successful lemma certifies rate optimality among all honest procedures, not only inverse-probability or nonrandomized intervals.

obligation.what_is_open: Prove the posterior-spread implication for the tilted weighted-erasure experiment uniformly over the stated conventional confidence levels and no-dominance arrays.
obligation.obstruction: The bridge to randomized original-data procedures is proved, but the current primitives do not supply the required biased weighted-Rademacher concentration-function estimate or the posterior missed-mass lower bound.
obligation.attempted: The likelihood-score and random-information route was audited. The orchestrator requires separate control of the exact factors \(1-t^2s_l^2\), compact tilt boundaries, and both conditional-noise regimes; those steps cannot be replaced by the previously rejected repeated-step argument.
obligation.partial_result: The tilted family is interior under the displayed no-dominance condition, and \(\mathrm{lem{:}hard\text{-}subexperiment\text{-}embedding}\) transfers pointwise coverage and expected length for every externally randomized rule.  What remains is the posterior-spread inequality itself: a future proof must establish a biased weighted-Rademacher concentration-function bound with conditional variances \(\sum_{K_l=0}w_l^2(1-t^2s_l^2)/4\), control compact-support endpoints, and compute posterior missed mass in both the small-conditional-noise and large-conditional-noise regimes.
